withheldByPolicy.why: we hold no headcount for any company. `companies.entity_type` names a KIND (company / research_org / other), never a size, and inventing a band from it would be a guess graded as a fact. 147 comparators stay dark.
no filed accounts anywhere in the corpus. 25 comparators stay dark.
no filed accounts anywhere in the corpus. 4 comparators stay dark.
no TRL or maturity fact about a company. The only proxy — which programmes it has won — is award data and would read the answer.
aid intensity is a property of the SCHEME, not of the applicant's willingness to co-finance. Deriving it from the won award's intensity would let the intensity signal grade itself.

derivable in principle from `private_funding_events` — a source no public award appears in, so it could not leak — but that table is not in `public/data/companies_index.json`, the one committed artifact this resolver may read. A build gate may not depend on gitignored data. 12 comparators; the honest fix is upstream in the index build.
nothing in the corpus states whether a company has a lender.
no ownership or shareholding data. The linked-enterprise half of the SME test cannot be answered for anyone.
no ultimate-control data. Note the corpus is Europe-scoped, so answering `no` for everyone would look right and would be an assumption, not a fact.
derived by sanitizeEligibility from exclusionFlags, which is itself withheld. No accounts, so the undertaking-in-difficulty test cannot be answered.

the GBER and de minimis exclusions are self-declared and nothing in the register records them for a beneficiary. Pinning `none` would be an ANSWER — the permissive one — asserted on behalf of 7,095 companies we have not asked.
a stated willingness, not a fact. Nothing states it.
a stance about the future. Its job is the CURE on an establishment blocker, and the harness grades retrieval, not advice.
a founder's own timing. The award's grant date is when the money arrived, not when they needed it, and it is on the won award.
